A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QuantV2X and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original perception experiments on DAIR-V2X, V2X-Real, and OPV2V, together with quantization ablations, latency measurements, and power measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds online V2X-ReaLO evaluation, system-component comparisons, and further quantization and alignment ablations.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline, codebook objectives, calibration algorithm, and heterogeneity/spatial alignment losses remain unchanged. Section 2.3 newly explains Gumbel-Softmax training weights and hard inference selections, but does not establish a change to the previously described procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds online perception evaluation through ROS-bag streaming on V2X-ReaLO across V2V, I2I, and V2I modes (Appendix E.2, Table 12). This substantially extends evaluation beyond static and simulated-latency accuracy settings. v1 already discussed the deployment platform and measured latency, but did not report this online accuracy evaluation.

E2.justification: The external baseline suites, including Where2comm, CodeFilling, PD-Quant, and LiDAR-PTQ, remain. v2 adds an explicit model-quantization-only control to the system comparison in Figure 6 and additional naive-rounding configurations in Table 11, providing limited extensions of the evaluated comparator configurations.

E3.justification: New protocols include INT2/8 evaluation, AP70 assessment by distance, four system configurations across three fusion architectures, and offline-versus-online evaluation on V2X-ReaLO. Existing training/calibration budgets and the simulated communication-delay protocol remain unchanged. These additions substantially expand evaluation design without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained calibration, alignment, codebook, and pose-error studies, v2 adds computation-versus-communication decomposition (Figure 6), a 2-bit failure test (Table 5), and analyses of AdaRound/alignment complementarity using strict localization metrics and naive-rounding controls (Tables 10-11). These directly test previously underexamined component roles and operating limits.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averaging latency over 10 runs, in v1 Appendix D.1 and v2 Appendix E.1. v2 adds no seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Most matched results remain unchanged, including Tables 1-3 and power measurements. v2 adds online QuantV2X mAP30/50 results of 50.1/40.1, 58.0/45.7, and 45.9/36.6 for V2V, I2I, and V2I, plus decomposition and alignment results and INT2/8 AP30/50 of 40.8/37.0. One retained codebook-ablation value changes: system mAP50 for 128 codes and one selection rises from 41.9 to 42.2 (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 14), matching the main table.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(10) are retained, with only equivalent notation changes. The new computation-latency grouping restates the existing latency decomposition. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the first fully quantized intermediate-fusion system, near-full-precision accuracy, 3.2-fold latency reduction, a +9.5 mAP30 gain, and improved scaling under memory constraints. New experiments support these existing claims; the revised conclusion emphasizes the deployment focus already present in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix D.5 adds a focused explanation of rounding-bias accumulation and complementary AdaRound/alignment roles, including stronger language about reaching a globally optimized state. Appendix E.2 acknowledges that intertwined online error sources limit attribution. Existing V2X-ViT and 2-bit limitations remain discussed, although the dedicated main-text limitations paragraph is removed.

D1.justification: v2 explains how codebook weights are generated through Gumbel-Softmax, explicitly specifies nL=128 and nR=1, and documents Gaussian positional/heading perturbations for the retained robustness experiment. It also describes ROS-bag packaging for online evaluation. These improve documentation; the established hardware, training budgets, and promised code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds STAMP to the cooperative-perception discussion and bibliography. The broader positioning against communication-only optimization remains unchanged. Moving related work to Appendix A and updating citation styles or publication metadata do not introduce additional substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 moves related work into the appendix, places references before the appendices, reorders model-level appendix material, and makes localized explanatory and terminology edits. It also updates author/contact information and adds acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different document template with changed typography, margins, headers, and float placement. It redraws the overview, adds the two-panel decomposition Figure 6 and Tables 5 and 10-12, and rearranges retained displays. The scaling plot's axis notation changes from mAP0.3 to equivalent mAP30 without changing its results.

improvement.justification: v1 supported deployment claims mainly through measured timing and simulated-latency accuracy. v2 adds online streaming evaluation across three collaboration modes and controls testing model/communication contributions and alignment at stricter precision thresholds. This substantially strengthens the central deployment argument and exposes operating limits. The new global-optimization language exceeds the formal evidence, and online attribution remains confounded, but these limitations do not outweigh the improved experimental support.
